clue.text: Insects bound to appear in a small desert town

parts.note: lice are small parasitic insects
to bound is to leap, so bounds are springs

explanation.surface: Swarms of leaping insects arrive somewhere out in the desert.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue lists the insects and the bounds first, but the A from 'a' leads the answer; 'to appear in' is just linking.
explanation.definitionFit: Alice Springs is a remote town in the middle of the Australian outback, a desert region.

clue.text: Wellingtons brought out for this event? Wind's on the way!

definitions.text: Wellingtons brought out for this event?

parts.note: air is moving wind, so wind's gives air's
how means the way something is done

explanation.surface: Rubber boots are pulled out for a soggy outdoor event as the wind picks up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wellingtons' look like rubber boots, but they were bombers, aircraft that would be on display.
explanation.definitionFit: Vickers Wellingtons were Second World War bombers, so they would be flown out for a display of aircraft.

clue.text: Analysis put into final plot before French director raised objection

parts.note: to inter is to bury, placing someone in their last resting place
pre is a prefix meaning before
Jacques Tati was a French film director

indicators.note: raised in a down answer means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: no is an objection

explanation.surface: A critic's analysis notes that the ending was buried before a French director raised his objection.
explanation.definitionFit: An interpretation is an explanation or reading of meaning, which is what analysis gives.

clue.text: Demanding to send down street artist

indicators.note: to send down in a down answer means shifting letters to the bottom

parts.note: stern means strict and demanding

explanation.surface: A demanding artist insists on being sent down the street.
explanation.walkthrough: Max ERNST was a German Surrealist painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Max Ernst was a German-born painter and leading figure of the Dada and Surrealist movements.

clue.text: Vote to include one for each government archive

indicators.note: to include means the vote word takes the other pieces inside it

parts.note: a poll is a vote
I is the Roman numeral one
per means for each

explanation.surface: A vote is held on adding one more item per department to the government's records.
explanation.walkthrough: The Pipe Rolls are medieval English Exchequer accounts.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pipe Rolls were the annual financial records of the medieval English Exchequer, kept as state papers.

clue.text: Online engine providing tips to display

indicators.note: tips means tilts over, so in a down answer the run is turned upside down
to display means the letters are shown inside the word providing

explanation.surface: A search engine on the web supplies helpful tips on screen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Online' looks like the internet, but means running on a railway line: Ivor the Engine was a Welsh steam train in a British children's TV series.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivor the Engine was a little green locomotive in a British children's television series, a railway engine on a line.

clue.text: Try one kiss, dissembling symptom of revulsion

parts.note: a go is a try or attempt

indicators.note: dissembling means disguising, so the letters are rearranged out of recognition

explanation.surface: Someone gives a kiss a try while hiding their disgust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dissembling' rearranges ONEKISS into OSESKIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Goose skin is goosebumps, the bristling of skin that can come with fear or disgust.

clue.text: One made a pop with this break

definitions.text: One made a pop with this break

parts.words: One made a pop with this break
parts.note: pop is a father, so someone just made a dad takes this time off work

explanation.surface: Someone causes a popping noise by breaking something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pop' sounds like a bang and 'break' like a fracture; they are a father and a holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: Paternity leave is time off work granted to a new father after his child is born.

clue.text: Variety of rock one's discovered in Scottish castle

parts.note: glam rock is a flamboyant 1970s style of rock music
one is I, and one's is a contraction of one is, giving IS

explanation.surface: A geologist finds an unusual type of rock inside a Scottish castle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rock' suggests geology; it is music.
explanation.definitionFit: Glamis Castle in Angus is a famous Scottish castle, linked with Macbeth and the Queen Mother's family.

clue.text: A number alongside pitch turned grass up

indicators.note: turned tells us the number and the pitch are read from right to left

parts.note: NO is the short form of number, as in No 10
pitch is black tar

explanation.surface: Someone's lawn is dug up beside a sports pitch, with a number marked next to it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grass' looks like lawn, but here it is slang for informing; NOTAR read from right to left gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To grass someone up is British slang for informing on them, the same as betraying them to the police.

clue.text: Occasion for shooting stars burning gaseous elements in cloud

indicators.note: in puts the heat and the gases inside the cloud

parts.note: a pall is a dark cloud, as of smoke
burning means very hot
O for oxygen and C for carbon, the elements that make up gases such as carbon monoxide
O for oxygen and C for carbon, the elements that make up gases such as carbon monoxide

explanation.surface: Shooting stars burn up as gases in the clouds high above.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shooting stars' suggests meteors; here celebrities are being photographed. 'in' puts the burning and the two element symbols inside the cloud word.
explanation.definitionFit: A photo call is an arranged session where celebrities pose for press photographers, so the famous are shot by cameras.

clue.text: Feminist records track others reproduced previously

indicators.note: previously places the reworked others before the track
reproduced means the letters of others are copied out in a new order

parts.note: RY is short for railway, a track

explanation.surface: Feminist archives log what other people recorded on a track long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reproduced' rearranges OTHERS into HERSTO.
explanation.definitionFit: Herstory is a feminist coinage for history written from women's perspective, recording their lives and achievements.

clue.text: Something to send you to sleep involving extra pill for one, and music

indicators.note: for says one thing stands in place of another, so the pill letter replaces the one

parts.words: Something to send you to sleep
parts.note: tedium is boredom, which makes you nod off
I is the Roman numeral one
E is slang for an ecstasy pill

explanation.surface: A sleeping aid now includes an extra pill per person, plus some soothing music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involving' just links: E takes the place of I in TEDIUM.
explanation.definitionFit: The Te Deum is a Latin hymn of praise, often set to music by composers such as Handel.

clue.text: In theory, shortcut in space around Golden Mile is complete

indicators.note: around tells us the complete word goes around the gold and the mile

parts.note: complete means entire or whole
OR is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A shortcut around London's Golden Mile is finally finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Golden' gives the heraldic word for gold, a common crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: A wormhole is a hypothetical tunnel through spacetime linking distant points, so physics theory makes it a cosmic shortcut.

clue.text: Toilet has strange instrument with mirror

indicators.note: strange means odd, so the letters are put in an unusual order

explanation.surface: The bathroom houses an odd gadget with a mirror on it.
explanation.definitionFit: A heliostat is a device with a moving mirror that keeps reflecting sunlight in one fixed direction.

clue.text: Despicable folk ruined singular surrounds close to park

indicators.note: surrounds says the ruined and singular letters go around the next piece

parts.note: sunk means done for, ruined

indicators.note: close to means the final letter of park

parts.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular

explanation.surface: Nasty people in a sorry state hang around near the park gates.
explanation.walkthrough: K goes in after the first S of SUNKS.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling people skunks is an insult for contemptible, unpleasant types, like the smelly animal.

clue.text: Wise old party animal?

parts.note: politic means prudent or wise

explanation.surface: Is a sensible older person really a big partygoer?
explanation.walkthrough: 'party animal' suggests a reveller; it is someone devoted to a political party.
explanation.definitionFit: A politico is a politician or political activist, someone whose life revolves around party politics.

clue.text: Lots of missing relations

definitions.meaning: countless, too many to count, as in riches beyond counting
not related, a relation being a telling or account, so never told

explanation.surface: Plenty of family members have gone missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relations' looks like family, but it is accounts or tellings: a story that was never related.
explanation.definitionFit: Untold means both innumerable, as in vast wealth, and not narrated or recounted to anyone.

clue.text: American university appearing on Cheers and Dynasty

parts.note: ta is British slang for thanks, like cheers
the Han dynasty ruled ancient China

explanation.surface: A US college shows up in the TV sitcom Cheers and the soap Dynasty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheers' and 'Dynasty' look like American TV shows; they are thanks and a Chinese dynasty.
explanation.definitionFit: A Utahan is a resident of the state of Utah, so a citizen of the United States.

clue.text: Ripping poncho a couple of times when rambling

indicators.note: rambling means wandering about, so the letters wander into a new order

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time, so two of them give TT

explanation.surface: A hiker's poncho gets torn a couple of times on a country walk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ripping' looks like tearing, but it is old slang for splendid.
explanation.definitionFit: Ripping is dated British slang for excellent, and top-notch means of the highest quality.

clue.text: Speaker's to keep greeting in store for farmer, perhaps

indicators.note: speaker's tells us we hear the phrase spoken rather than written

parts.note: to keep hailing someone is to hail them often, hail oft

explanation.surface: The Commons Speaker likes to keep a greeting in reserve for a farmer.
explanation.definitionFit: A hayloft is the upper storage room of a barn where a farmer keeps fodder, perhaps as one example.

clue.text: Originate all the same, endless vibes externally

indicators.note: externally says the shortened vibes word sits on the outside
endless means the final letter is cut off the vibes word

parts.note: an aura is the vibes given off by a person or place
tho is a short spelling of though, meaning all the same

explanation.surface: A creator insists the atmosphere stays unchanged, all good vibes on the outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' drops the last letter of the vibes word, leaving AUR, and 'externally' wraps that around the clipped spelling of though.
explanation.definitionFit: To author something is to create or originate it, as a writer brings a book into being.

clue.text: Are the perfect matches occurring in bouts?

definitions.meaning: things that are perfect matches suit each other completely
happening in irregular spells or spasms rather than steadily

explanation.surface: A question about whether ideal pairings only happen now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half splits into two words: perfect matches fit fully.
explanation.definitionFit: Fitfully means in irregular bursts, stopping and starting, like sleep broken into short spells.

clue.text: Scrap of paper found outside East London school?

indicators.note: found outside says the paper's letters wrap around the school

parts.note: FT is the Financial Times newspaper
an East End Cockney drops the H, so high school becomes 'igh

explanation.surface: A scrap of paper is found outside a school in London's East End.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrap of paper' reads as a piece; 'Scrap' alone is the definition, a brawl.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrap is an informal word for a brawl or scuffle.

clue.text: Doctor coming from county fair

parts.note: OK means fair or acceptable

explanation.surface: A medic arrives from the county show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like a medic, but here it is a verb meaning to falsify.
explanation.definitionFit: To cook the books is to falsify them, the same as doctoring figures.

clue.text: Castle with excellent fencing, or one with better grounds

indicators.note: fencing means enclosing, so the excellent letters surround the castle

parts.note: A1 means excellent, with the 1 read as the letter I
a fort is a fortified castle
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A well-fenced castle, or one standing on finer land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grounds' looks like estate land but means reasons.
explanation.definitionFit: A fortiori is a Latin phrase meaning with stronger reason, used when a conclusion follows even more firmly.

clue.text: Returning on a bit of summer business to aid growth

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the words are read from right to left

parts.note: Aug is August, a part of summer

explanation.surface: Coming back to summer trade to help the business grow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'business' looks commercial; it is a euphemism for droppings, and bird droppings feed plants.
explanation.definitionFit: Guano is seabird or bat excrement used as a rich fertiliser, so it helps crops grow.

clue.text: Chinatown street took two names, unusually

indicators.note: unusually means in an odd arrangement, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for name, so two of them give NN

explanation.surface: A street in Chinatown oddly took on two names.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chinatown' suggests a Chinese quarter, but here it is a town famous for china: STOKE-ON-TRENT is the English city of the Potteries.
explanation.definitionFit: Stoke-on-Trent is the heart of English pottery making, home to Wedgwood and Spode, so a town of china.
